newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-SPARTAK DROP PRECIOUS POINTS IN SIBERIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPARTAK DROP PRECIOUS POINTS IN SIBERIA.

text.p: Russian champions Spartak Moscow dropped their first points of the season on Saturday when they allowed newly-promoted Tyumen to snatch a couple of goals in the last 12 minutes for a 2-2 draw in Siberia.
The Muscovites stayed top with 10 points from four matches although Rotor Volgograd, third last season, beat Zenit 1-0 in St Petersburg to move level with Spartak on points.
Former Zenit striker Denis Zubko, who joined Volgograd in the close season, scored just before halftime.
Alania Vladikavkaz, 1996 runners up, recovered from two straight defeats with a comfortable 3-1 win over previously unbeaten Krylya Sovietov in Samara.

Alania, who had missed three penalties in two matches, were without striker Anatoly Kanishchev, who was handed a five-game ban on Friday for failing to appear for Russian international duty against Cyprus last week.
Another title contender, CSKA Moscow, had to salvage a 1-1 home draw against lowly Zhemchuzhina Sochi. CSKA's Vladimir Kulik equalised from the spot just five minutes from time.
KamAZ Chelny, with no points, no goals and 11 goals against after their first three games, restored some pride by toppling newcomers Shinnik Yaroslavl 3-0 at home.
